_note:
Suspect counts are a ratchet, not a score: they may only stop growing. The numbers below are the live
counts as of this commit, and the two movements that produced them are recorded here because a number nobody
can account for gets --update'd blind.

(1) The whole table fell twice in one round, and both falls have the same mechanism: **suspects are computed
only over the keys the UI uses**, so a dictionary entry that loses its last call site takes its suspects with
it. Nothing was "fixed"; 51 keys were retired.

   (1a) Retiring those 51 keys (the live-status page and the posting-a-danmaku surface: 9 + 20 keys, plus
        liveHint* 3, biliUidHint / needUid / sourceUid, shareCheck and llmFeat_live / llmFeat_danmaku) took
        their suspect rows with them. Every one of the 51 was verified to have had a call site at the commit
        before the removal, so none of them was already-dead code. The old baseline's per-locale numbers had
        been inflated by rows that were live then and are not now.
   (1b) The glossary also lost the three terms for the retired platform (bilibili / B站 / B 站). That term's
        "default wording is a Latin brand name" rule flagged every locale whose text mentions the platform
        and has no override for it, which is what the 14 fil-PH rows and most of the other counts were: the
        platform is no longer named anywhere in the UI, so those rows cannot exist. LATIN_DEFAULT_ALLOWED in
        tools/i18n-proofread.mjs no longer lists it for the same reason, and the two edits go together.

(2) One incident worth recording rather than accepting, because it was a real edit defect and it did NOT
    become a baseline: a stripping script that removed the retired keys from web/src/locales/overlays.js also
    ate locale-block closing braces, which silently deleted unrelated entries. It showed up as nine new th-TH
    "this row is really an English fallback" rows that had not been there before. The file was repaired and
    re-verified per key against HEAD (only the intended keys differ), and th-TH is back to 0. If a future
    change makes a fallback count jump in a locale whose layer nothing touched, that is this shape of defect,
    not a translation problem.
